name: Tamachi
tagline: Shinagawa in 5 minutes and Tokyo in 10 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Minato City, where JR East run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 15 minutes to Otemachi, 30 minutes to Shinjuku, 26 minutes to Shibuya and 5 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 3.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 4.2 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.7 m to 6.9 m, a difference of 4.2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 3 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. For storm surge, 6 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 14 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 愛育病院, about 8 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 芝公園かみやまクリニック, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: JR Yamanote Line and JR Keihin-Tohoku Line. Both lines are run by JR East, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: JR Keihin-Tohoku Line runs at 159% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大井町→品川, which this station is not on. JR Yamanote Line runs at 136%. Its busiest stretch is 新大久保→新宿, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000 and 2LDK ¥350,000 to ¥360,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. What pushes the figure up: plenty of places to eat out. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
